title: release-engineering-meeting-notes-2026-05-19
content:
Release Engineering Meeting Notes - 2026-05-19

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (release eng lead)
- Daniel Kim (platform eng)
- Sofia Martinez (serving runtime)
- Ben Carter (SRE)
- Lin Zhao (QA)
- Emma Johnson (product ops, observer)

Agenda:
1) Review last week's release train and hotfixes
2) Current canary and rollback status
3) Changelog highlights for v1.12.3 train
4) Post-mortem summary: intermittent KV cache eviction incident
5) Action items and next steps

1) Last week's recap
- Released v1.12.2 (minor bugfix + dependency bumps) on 2026-05-14. No customer-facing incidents. Canary metrics stable for 48h before full rollout.
- Hotfix RE-1420 applied on 2026-05-16 to address regression in tokenization logic introduced by a third-party tokenizer bump (GH PR #2294). Hotfix deployed to Dedicated pools and Private customers with zero rollback.
- Release-runner job failures observed during the weekend (flaky network to artifact store). Root cause: transient S3 qps throttling. Mitigation: rate-limit retry backoff increased and staging artifact replication added. (See linked JIRA RE-1445)

2) Current canary and rollback status
- Canary for v1.12.3 started 2026-05-18 09:00 UTC. Targets: 5% of hosted API traffic, select dedicated pools in us-west2.
- Early canary metrics: request success rate 99.94% (baseline 99.96%), median generation latency +12ms, p95 latency +35ms.
- Quality evals: prompt set regression tests show no material output degradation; embedding cosine stability checks within expected bounds.
- Two minor anomalies noted:
  - A slight increase in memory churn on shared-hosted nodes when long-context workloads hit the new KV-prefetch optimization. Tracing attached.
  - One dedicated customer reported elevated tail latency (investigating networking stack).
- Canary decision: continue canary to 24h full metrics window. If p95 stays < +50ms and error rate < 0.5% relative increase, proceed to 50% rollout.
- Rollback playbook: automatic rollback threshold set to a 1.5x increase in error rate or p95 +120ms. ON-CALL: Ben Carter.

3) Changelog highlights for v1.12.3 (planned full rollout after canary)
- Feature: KV-prefetch optimization for long-context chat sessions (serving-runtime) - reduces repeated KV loads on repeated prefixes, expected to cut token compute by ~8% on long sessions (Sofia).
- Fix: Tokenization edge-case handling for Unicode combining chars (hotfix lane, covered in RE-1420).
- Ops: Artifact replication to fallback buckets to mitigate S3 throttling during release-runner jobs.
- Dependency: PyTorch 2.2.1 -> 2.2.2 (minor patch). Verified against CI matrix.
- Observability: Added per-route token-level cost traces to the console (product-ops + observability).

4) Incident / post-mortem summary: KV cache eviction spikes (2026-05-12)
- Symptom: transient increase in latency and memory pressure on a subset of hosted infer nodes, correlated with a sudden traffic burst for long-chat sessions.
- Root cause: cache eviction threshold misconfiguration combined with a recent config change that shortened TTL for ephemeral prefixes.
- Impact: ~0.4% increased error rate for 45 minutes, self-healed after autoscaling.
- Remediation done: TTL reverted, eviction logic adjusted to be adaptive to long-context heuristics.
- Long-term actions: add synthetic load test for long-chat patterns, add alert on sustained cache eviction rate > 10/min.

5) Action items
- Aisha: finalize rollout runbook update to include automatic fallback to v1.12.2 for Dedicated customers. Due: 2026-05-20. (linked: confluence.redwood.com/display/RE/Release+Playbook)
- Ben: validate and harden rollback alarms in PagerDuty (threshold tuning + test trigger). Due: 2026-05-21.
- Sofia: add KV-prefetch memory telemetry and a short-term mitigator (limit prefetch window). Due: 2026-05-22.
- Lin: expand QA regression set with 10 additional long-context prompts (include edge Unicode cases). Due: 2026-05-21.
- Daniel: finalize artifact-store replication changes and coordinate with infra for increased staging capacity. Confirm through canary run. Due: 2026-05-20.

Notes / Misc:
- We flagged a potential compatibility risk for several Private deployment customers whose on-prem infra uses older GPU drivers. Product ops to send a compatibility advisory and opt-in testing instructions.
- Internal FYI: release-runner PR #2301 contains the replication logic; please review if you have bandwidth.

Decisions made:
- Proceed with extended 24h canary for v1.12.3 and re-evaluate at 2026-05-19 18:30 UTC.
- Keep hotfix branch protected until 2026-06-01 to ensure no regression re-introductions.

Next meeting:
- Weekly sync: 2026-05-26 17:00 UTC
- Check-in: canary decision update and hotfix review

End of notes.
